blocks.text: How Foreclosures & BC Supreme Court-Ordered Sales Work in Chilliwack

parts.t: In British Columbia, residential and agricultural foreclosures are sold through
BC Supreme Court-ordered sales
(typically heard at the Chilliwack Law Courts at 46085 Yale Road or New Westminster / Vancouver Supreme Court registries) after a lender obtains an Order Nisi and subsequent
Order for Conduct of Sale
. Active court-ordered listings in
Chilliwack
and
Sardis
are marketed on the MLS® just like standard properties, but the contract rules and court approval process are completely different.

blocks.text: First Acceptable Offer vs. Competing Sealed Bids in Court

parts.t: First, a buyer submits an offer with a
Court-Ordered Sale Schedule "A"
attached, which strips out standard seller warranties and specifies that the property is sold
"as-is, where-is"

on the possession date. Once the first buyer removes their inspection, financing, and title-search subjects, the lender's lawyer schedules a BC Supreme Court hearing date to approve that sale. Any competing buyers may submit
sealed, subject-free backup offers
in court on the morning of the hearing—meaning the first buyer's offer price becomes public in the court materials before the judge opens the sealed envelopes.

blocks.text: As-Is Risks, Tenancies, Property Disclosure & Financing Checklists

parts.t: Because the foreclosing bank has never lived in the property, you do
not

receive a Property Disclosure Statement (PDS), and appliances or chattels are not warranted. Before removing subjects (or before submitting a subject-free sealed bid at the courthouse), always conduct a professional home inspection, verify occupancy and BC
Residential Tenancy Act
obligations if a tenant is in place, check strata arrears or rural well/septic conditions, and confirm your mortgage lender will fund a court-ordered sale.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Foreclosures & Court-Ordered Sales Real Estate FAQs

parts.t: How does the BC Supreme Court foreclosure buying process work in Chilliwack?

After a lender obtains an Order for Conduct of Sale, the property is listed on the MLS®. The first buyer negotiates an accepted offer (subject to court approval) and removes their subjects. The lender's lawyer then sets a court hearing date. At the hearing, other buyers may submit unconditional sealed bids, and the master or judge approves the highest qualified offer.
Is it better to be the first offer or a competing sealed bidder in BC court?

Wait-and-bid sealed bidders have a strategic advantage because the first buyer's accepted price is disclosed in the public court application materials before the hearing, whereas competing sealed bidders keep their bid amounts private until the judge opens the envelopes. However, if no competing bidder shows up at court, the first buyer wins the property without competition.
Can a competing bidder at the courthouse include financing or inspection subjects?

No. Any competing bid submitted at the BC Supreme Court hearing must be completely unconditional (subject-free), accompanied by a certified cheque or bank draft deposit, and written with the lender's Schedule A attached. Any inspection and financing approval must be completed before the court date.
What does 'as-is, where-is' mean in a Chilliwack foreclosure Schedule A?

Schedule A overrides standard Contract of Purchase and Sale clauses so the lender makes no representations or warranties regarding the building's physical condition, environmental status, permits, appliances, or vacant possession if unauthorized occupants remain.
What happens if there aren't many active Chilliwack foreclosures listed today?

Court-ordered inventory in Chilliwack fluctuates month by month and properties often receive initial offers within days of listing. Contact Jared Gibbons at 604-928-1361 to receive immediate MLS® alerts the moment a new Conduct of Sale listing hits Chilliwack, Sardis, or the eastern Fraser Valley.
Can I get a standard mortgage on a foreclosure property in Chilliwack?

Yes, provided the property is in habitable condition with a functioning kitchen, bathroom, heating system, and safe roof/electrical. If the property has severe water damage, mould, or missing fixtures, you may need purchase-plus-improvements, credit union, or alternative/private bridge financing.
What happens if a tenant is living in a Chilliwack foreclosure property?

Under BC's Residential Tenancy Act, an existing lawful residential tenancy generally survives a foreclosure sale unless the court order specifically grants vacant possession on the grounds that the occupant is the foreclosed borrower or a non-arm's-length occupant. Always review the court filings and tenancy status before bidding.
